shelves.label: K · First words in every book
shelves.teachingPoint: the earliest ten — no family, no rule to hang them on; these are simply the words a child meets on page one of every book

shelves.label: K · When o goes its own way
shelves.teachingPoint: o says /u/ or /oo/ in exactly the place the code taught so far predicts a short o

shelves.label: K · When w changes the a
shelves.teachingPoint: after a w the letter a says /o/ — want, wash, watch, swan; the w does it every time

shelves.label: Grade 1 · Words that end in ve
shelves.teachingPoint: no English word ends in v, so a job-less e is added — and unlike a real magic e it does not lengthen the vowel

shelves.label: Grade 1 · The /oo/ words that hide an l
shelves.teachingPoint: oul says /oo/ with the l silent; the silent-w words sit beside them as cousins

shelves.label: Grade 1 · Vowels that say /e/
shelves.teachingPoint: ai, ie, ea, ay and a all landing on the short /e/ sound

shelves.label: Grade 1 · Words that land on /air/
shelves.teachingPoint: ere, eir and ear all landing on /air/ — three spellings, one sound

shelves.label: Grade 1 · Counting words
shelves.teachingPoint: the number words are irregular as a class — four, eight, five, twelve, eleven

shelves.label: Grade 2 · Letters that stay silent
shelves.teachingPoint: silent k, silent l, silent b, silent w, silent t, and the gh hiding inside igh

shelves.label: Grade 2 · r-words that change
shelves.teachingPoint: ear, or and ere all landing on /er/ — learn, work, were

shelves.label: Grade 2 · Long words we meet often
shelves.teachingPoint: multi-syllable high-frequency words; the unstressed schwa is never the heart, only the part that truly breaks the code

shelves.label: Grade 2 · Words that sound the same
shelves.teachingPoint: five homophone pairs — the sound is shared, so the spelling is the only thing left to remember

words.note: the e says /uh/
words.heartOverride: a lone e says /e/ everywhere else the child has met it — here it is the weak /uh/
words.sentence: The cat sat on my lap.

words.note: the f says /v/ — the only word in English where it does
words.heartOverride: f says /f/ in every other word; this one word is the exception
words.sentence: I drank all of my milk.

words.note: the o says /oo/
words.heartOverride: a lone o says /o/ as in on — /oo/ is not a rule the child has been given
words.sentence: We run to the bus.

words.note: the o says /oo/, like in to
words.heartOverride: same handful as to — the o is doing a job no rule predicts
words.sentence: What can you do with a ball?

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w — the s saying /z/ is an ordinary rule, not the heart
words.heartOverride: the w-changes-a pattern is not taught until later; here only the a is unexpected
words.sentence: My dog was fast asleep.

words.note: ai usually says /ay/ — here it says /e/
words.sentence: Hello, said the little bird.

words.note: ou usually says /ow/ — here it says /oo/
words.sentence: Can you see the moon?

words.note: the ve keeps the a short — this e is not a magic e
words.heartOverride: elsewhere in the bank ve simply follows the vowel it is given; in have it is the whole reason the word looks long and sounds short
words.sentence: I have a warm hat.

words.note: the o says /u/
words.heartOverride: o for /u/ is not a rule the child has been given
words.sentence: Come and see my cake!

words.note: the o says /u/, like in come
words.heartOverride: same o as come — unpredictable from the code taught so far
words.sentence: I will pick some flowers.

words.note: the o does the work of two sounds: /w/ + /u/
words.heartOverride: one letter carrying two sounds happens in no other word the child knows
words.sentence: I can see one star.

words.note: wh says just /h/ here — and the o is the same o as in to and do
words.heartOverride: wh says /w/ in where and everywhere; who is the word where the w disappears
words.sentence: Who left the door open?

words.note: oe says /u/ — the s saying /z/ is an ordinary rule, not the heart
words.sentence: Does your cat like to nap?

words.note: the o says /u/
words.heartOverride: o for /u/ is unpredictable — from looks exactly like frog and sounds nothing like it
words.sentence: Where do you come from?

words.note: the o says /wu/, like in one — the c saying /s/ before e is an ordinary rule
words.heartOverride: the same two-sounds-in-one-letter o as in one
words.sentence: Once I saw a big bear!

words.note: the o says /u/
words.heartOverride: everything else in month follows the code; only the o refuses
words.sentence: We go swimming once a month.

words.note: the o says /u/, so nothing does not rhyme with not
words.heartOverride: not and nothing share their first three letters and part company on this o
words.sentence: There is nothing in my lunchbox.

words.note: the o says /u/
words.heartOverride: front looks like it should rhyme with pond — the o is the reason it does not
words.sentence: Sit at the front of the bus.

words.note: the o says /oo/ as in book, not /o/ as in on
words.heartOverride: the short-oo sound has no single-o spelling rule at this stage
words.sentence: A grey wolf stood by the trees.

words.note: the o says /u/ at the very start of the word
words.heartOverride: over and oven differ by one letter and the o changes sound completely
words.sentence: The buns are hot in the oven.

words.note: the a says /o/ because a w comes first
words.heartOverride: the w-controlled a is a Grade 1 rule — at this stage the a is simply unexpected
words.sentence: I want to go on the boat.

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w — wash does not rhyme with cash
words.heartOverride: cash, dash and mash all say /a/; only the w changes it
words.sentence: We wash the dog in the garden.

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w — watch does not rhyme with catch
words.heartOverride: catch and watch look like a pair and are not one
words.sentence: I watch the birds from my window.

words.note: the a says /o/ — swan does not rhyme with man
words.heartOverride: the w works through the sw blend too, which no rule has told the child yet
words.sentence: A white swan swims on the lake.

words.note: the a says /o/ — swap sounds like stop, not like slap
words.heartOverride: slap and swap differ by one letter and by the whole vowel
words.sentence: Shall we swap seats?

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w — wand does not rhyme with hand
words.heartOverride: hand, band and land all say /a/; wand does not
words.sentence: The fairy waves her wand.

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w
words.heartOverride: clasp and wasp look like rhymes and are not
words.sentence: A wasp landed on my plate.

words.note: the a says /o/ — swamp rhymes with stomp
words.heartOverride: camp and swamp are one letter apart and rhyme with different words
words.sentence: Frogs like the muddy swamp.

words.note: the a says /o/ after the w
words.heartOverride: raffle and waffle are a rhyme in spelling only
words.sentence: I put honey on my waffle.

words.note: the u after q makes a w sound, and that w changes the a to /o/
words.heartOverride: the w hiding inside qu does the same job as a written w
words.sentence: This squash is big and yellow.

words.note: the ve keeps the i short — no English word ends in v, so an e was added with no job
words.heartOverride: everywhere else a final e lengthens the vowel; after v it does nothing at all
words.sentence: I will give my train to the baby.

words.note: the ve keeps the i short, like in give
words.heartOverride: the job-less e is the whole point of the word and no rule predicts it
words.sentence: Do frogs live in the pond?

words.note: the o says /u/ — the e cannot help it
words.heartOverride: the ve is ordinary here; it is the o that breaks the code
words.sentence: I love my soft rabbit.

words.note: the o says /oo/, not its name
words.heartOverride: love and move are spelt alike and the o differs in both from the code and from each other
words.sentence: Can you move that chair?

words.note: the o says /u/, so above rhymes with love
words.heartOverride: o for /u/ is the same unpredictable o as in love and come
words.sentence: The kite flies above the trees.

words.note: the o says /u/ — glove rhymes with love, not with stove
words.heartOverride: stove and glove are one letter apart and the o goes two different ways
words.sentence: I lost one glove in the snow.

words.note: both vowels stay short and the final e has no job
words.heartOverride: a two-syllable word ending in a silent e that changes nothing is not predictable at Grade 1
words.sentence: There is one olive left.

words.note: the e after v does nothing — ur already has the sound
words.heartOverride: a magic e after an r-controlled vowel would normally change it; here it cannot
words.sentence: The path makes a big curve.

words.note: the e after v does nothing — er already has the sound
words.heartOverride: the e looks like it should be doing something and is only there to keep the v company
words.sentence: Dad will serve us lunch.

words.note: ee has already said /ee/, so the last e is only there because v cannot end a word
words.heartOverride: three vowels in a row where only the first two speak
words.sentence: There is a hole in my sleeve.

words.note: oul says /oo/ and the l is silent
words.sentence: Would you like an apple?

words.note: oul says /oo/, like in would
words.sentence: Could you hold my ball?

words.note: the would, could, should family all share oul
words.sentence: We should feed the fish.

words.note: the w is silent in front of the r
words.heartOverride: w is a spoken sound in every other word the child knows; before r it vanishes
words.sentence: I write my name with a pencil.

words.note: the w is silent, just as in write
words.heartOverride: same silent w before r — nothing in the code predicts it
words.sentence: She wrote a book about bears.

words.note: the w is silent — wrong begins with the same sound as rong would
words.heartOverride: the silent w before r is a spelling memory, never a sound
words.sentence: I turned the wrong way.

words.note: the w is silent — wrap and rap sound exactly alike
words.heartOverride: two spellings for one sound, told apart only by this silent w
words.sentence: Let us wrap the present.

words.note: the w is silent in front of the r
words.heartOverride: the silent w is the only part of wrist a child cannot sound out
words.sentence: The band goes round my wrist.

words.note: the w is silent in the middle of the word
words.heartOverride: a silent w buried mid-word, where nothing marks it
words.sentence: I know the answer to that.

words.note: the w is silent — sword sounds like sord
words.heartOverride: the sw blend speaks in swan and swim; in sword the w is silent
words.sentence: The wooden sword is light.

words.note: ai says /e/, like in said
words.heartOverride: ai says /ay/ in rain and train; said and again are the pair that do not
words.sentence: Read me that book again!

words.note: ie says /e/ — there is an i hiding in friend
words.heartOverride: ie says /ee/ in field and /y/ in pie; /e/ happens only here
words.sentence: My friend has a big dog.

words.note: the a says /e/ — many does not rhyme with canny
words.heartOverride: a for /e/ appears in only two common words, many and any
words.sentence: How many grapes can you count?

words.note: the a says /e/, like in many
words.heartOverride: the twin of many — the same unpredictable a
words.sentence: Is there any milk left?

words.note: ay says /e/ here, though say says /ay/
words.heartOverride: ay says /ay/ in day, play and say itself; adding one s changes the vowel
words.sentence: The duck says quack.

words.note: ea says /e/ here, not /ee/
words.heartOverride: ea says /ee/ in sea and read; the short /e/ has to be met word by word
words.sentence: I put my hat on my head.

words.note: ea says /e/ — bread and bead differ by one letter and by the whole vowel
words.heartOverride: the short-e ea family is learnt word by word, never by rule
words.sentence: We share the warm bread.

words.note: ea says /e/ — the final y saying /ee/ is an ordinary rule
words.heartOverride: read and ready share four letters and split on this ea
words.sentence: Are you ready to go home?

words.note: ea says /e/
words.heartOverride: one of the short-e ea words that must be met one at a time
words.sentence: A peacock feather is bright blue.

words.note: ea says /e/ — a sweater is not a sweeter
words.heartOverride: the same short-e ea, and here it changes the word entirely
words.sentence: My sweater keeps me warm.

words.note: ere says /air/
words.sentence: Look, there is a fish!

words.note: ere says /air/, like in there
words.sentence: Where is my other shoe?

words.note: eir says /air/ — a third spelling for the same sound
words.sentence: This is their red car.

words.note: eir says /air/ — the s on the end behaves as usual
words.sentence: The blue tent is theirs.

words.note: ear says /air/ here, not /eer/
words.sentence: A big bear walks in the forest.

words.note: ear says /air/ — a pear is not a peer
words.sentence: I ate a juicy pear.

words.note: ear says /air/, so wear rhymes with bear
words.sentence: I wear my boots in the rain.

words.note: ear says /air/ when tear means to rip
words.sentence: Do not tear the paper.

words.note: ere says /air/, exactly as it does in where
words.sentence: There are leaves everywhere!

words.note: ere says /air/ — the where inside nowhere keeps its sound
words.sentence: My sock is nowhere to be found.

words.note: the three letters our work together to say /or/
words.sentence: I can count four ducks.

words.note: our says /or/, just as it does in four
words.sentence: Our class has fourteen children.

words.note: eigh says /ay/ — four letters, one sound
words.sentence: The clock says eight.

words.note: eigh says /ay/, as in eight
words.sentence: My sister is eighteen today.

words.note: eigh says /ay/ — the final y saying /ee/ is an ordinary rule
words.sentence: Grandpa is eighty years old.

words.note: the i says its name here, unlike in give and live
words.heartOverride: ve normally keeps the vowel short; five is the number that refuses
words.sentence: I have five fingers on one hand.

words.note: the e on the end has no job — v may not finish a word
words.heartOverride: the child sees a magic e and must learn it changes nothing after v
words.sentence: I stacked twelve blocks.

words.note: the first e says /i/, not /e/
words.heartOverride: three e letters in one word and the first one alone changes sound
words.sentence: There are eleven cows in the field.

words.note: the o says /u/ — a dozen rhymes with cousin
words.heartOverride: o for /u/ again, in a counting word the child hears long before reading
words.sentence: We baked a dozen muffins.

words.note: ou says /u/ here, not /ow/
words.heartOverride: ou says /ow/ in cloud and out; /u/ has to be met word by word
words.sentence: A couple of birds sat on the wall.

words.note: the k is silent in front of the n
words.heartOverride: k speaks in kite and kick; before n it is written and never said
words.sentence: I bumped my knee on the step.

words.note: the k is silent, just as in knee
words.heartOverride: the silent k before n is a spelling memory with no sound at all
words.sentence: The knife is too sharp for me.

words.note: the gh inside igh has gone completely silent
words.heartOverride: igh is read as one chunk precisely because its g and h say nothing
words.sentence: Put up your right hand.

words.note: the b at the end is silent
words.heartOverride: b is a strong sound everywhere else; after m at the end of a word it disappears
words.sentence: A little lamb sleeps in the grass.

words.note: the b is silent, as in lamb
words.heartOverride: the silent b after m has to be remembered, never heard
words.sentence: My thumb is shorter than my finger.

words.note: the b is silent — and the o says its name with nothing to help it
words.heartOverride: comb and bomb are spelt alike and the b is silent in both, while the vowels part company
words.sentence: I comb my hair each morning.

words.note: the b is silent — climb rhymes with time
words.heartOverride: a written b that makes no sound at the end of the word
words.sentence: We climb the mountain slowly.

words.note: the l is silent
words.heartOverride: l is a sound in lamp and milk; between a and f it is written and not said
words.sentence: I ate half of my apple.

words.note: the l is silent, as it is in half and talk
words.heartOverride: the silent l before k is a small family the child must simply collect
words.sentence: We walk the dog every day.

words.note: the t is silent between the s and the e
words.heartOverride: a silent t buried inside the word, with nothing to mark it
words.sentence: Listen to the loud drum!

words.note: ear says /er/, not /eer/ and not /air/
words.heartOverride: ear has already been met as /air/ in bear and pear; this third sound is new
words.sentence: We learn about the moon.

words.note: ear says /er/ at the very start of the word
words.heartOverride: the same three letters as bear and hear, and a third sound again
words.sentence: The earth spins round the sun.

words.note: ear says /er/ — heard and hear look alike and do not rhyme
words.heartOverride: adding one letter to hear changes the vowel completely
words.sentence: I heard a bird sing.

words.note: ear says /er/ — the final y saying /ee/ is an ordinary rule
words.heartOverride: the /er/ reading of ear must be met word by word
words.sentence: We got up early to see the sunrise.

words.note: ear says /er/, so search rhymes with church
words.heartOverride: nothing in the spelling shows which of the three ear sounds is wanted
words.sentence: We search for the missing sock.

words.note: or says /er/ after a w, not /or/
words.heartOverride: or says /or/ in fork and corn; the w in front of it changes the sound
words.sentence: We work together in the garden.

words.note: or says /er/ after the w — word and cord do not rhyme
words.heartOverride: one letter in front decides which sound or takes
words.sentence: I wrote one word on the whiteboard.

words.note: or says /er/ after the w
words.heartOverride: the w-changes-or family has to be collected word by word
words.sentence: The globe shows the whole world.

words.note: or says /er/ after the w — a worm is not warm
words.heartOverride: worm and warm swap their vowel letters and swap sounds the other way
words.sentence: A worm wriggles in the wet mud.

words.note: ere says /er/ here, though it says /air/ in there and where
words.heartOverride: the same three letters as there and where, and a different sound
words.sentence: We were very quiet in the hall.

words.note: eo says /ee/ — the o is along for the ride
words.heartOverride: eo appears in almost no other word a child will meet
words.sentence: Lots of people ride the bus.

words.note: au says /u/ here, not /or/ — the s saying /z/ is an ordinary rule
words.heartOverride: au says /or/ in sauce and haunt; because is the word where it does not
words.sentence: I like the sun because it is warm.

words.note: the o says /u/ — the first a is only a schwa and is not the heart
words.heartOverride: o for /u/ again, in the middle of a long word
words.sentence: May I have another cookie?

words.note: the o says /u/ — brother does not rhyme with both
words.heartOverride: both and brother share oth and the o goes two different ways
words.sentence: My brother is taller than me.

words.note: the o says /u/
words.heartOverride: the o in the mother, brother, other family is unpredictable every time
words.sentence: My mother reads to me at bedtime.

words.note: the o says /u/ right at the start
words.heartOverride: an opening o that says /u/ with nothing at all to signal it
words.sentence: The other shoe is under my bed.

words.note: the a says /or/ after the w
words.heartOverride: later and water rhyme in spelling and not in sound
words.sentence: The water is cold on my feet.

words.note: the a says /ar/ without an r to make it
words.heartOverride: gather and father are one letter apart and the a says two different things
words.sentence: My father makes soup for us.

words.note: the o says its name and the e says nothing at all
words.heartOverride: a long o with no marker, plus a silent e stranded before the s
words.sentence: I fold my clothes and put them away.

words.note: the s says /sh/ and the u says /oo/
words.heartOverride: s says /sh/ in almost no other word, and the u beside it is just as unexpected
words.sentence: There is too much sugar in this tea.

words.note: ear says /eer/ here — this is the hear you do with your ears
words.heartOverride: the third sound of ear, after /air/ in bear and /er/ in learn
words.sentence: Can you hear the rain?

words.note: ere says /eer/ here, though it says /air/ in there and where
words.heartOverride: the same ere as there and where, saying something else again
words.sentence: Come and sit here beside me.

words.note: the k is silent — this is the know that means to understand
words.heartOverride: the silent k is the only thing telling know apart from no in writing
words.sentence: I know the way home.

words.note: the o says its name with nothing to help it — this is the no that means not any
words.heartOverride: a lone o at the end of a word saying its name is not yet a rule the child has
words.sentence: There is no milk left in the jug.

words.note: the w is silent — it is there to show this is the number
words.heartOverride: a silent w that exists only to mark which of the three sound-alikes this is
words.sentence: I have two carrots for the pot.

words.note: oo does its usual job — it is the doubled o that marks this as the too meaning also
words.heartOverride: the sound gives no clue at all; only the doubled o says which word this is
words.sentence: May I come too?

words.note: the o says /u/ — this is the son in a family
words.heartOverride: o for /u/, and it is also the letter that tells son from sun
words.sentence: Her son is in my class.

words.note: the u is the plain spelling of /u/ — this is the sun in the sky
words.heartOverride: the vowel sounds the same as in son; only this letter says which word is meant
words.sentence: The sun is warm on my face.

words.note: ee is the spelling that marks this as the been of have been
words.heartOverride: ee and ea sound alike here, so the choice between them must be remembered
words.sentence: We have been to the farm.

words.note: ea is the spelling that marks this as the bean you can eat
words.heartOverride: nothing in the sound chooses ea over ee; the word must be known by sight
words.sentence: One bean grew into a tall plant.
